families.family_name: OH-rich biopolymer matrix + water-processable film-forming co-binder + 1-D nanochannel clay + complexed phosphoric-acid phase
families.family_description: This quaternary archetype combines a hydrogen-bond-rich biopolymer, a film-forming co-binder that suppresses brittleness, a 1-D fibrous or tubular clay that provides percolated nanoconfinement, and a phosphoric-acid-derived proton phase plasticised against crystallisation. It is well aligned with cold-side operation because bound water, interfacial water, and co-solvent-assisted acid speciation can remain mobile below 273 K while the hybrid scaffold reduces phase segregation.
descriptor_match: D1: Percolated polymer/clay/acid network can avoid bulk-like freezing by confining the conducting phase and distributing it across continuous interfaces.
D2: Biopolymer OH groups, clay-bound water, and anti-freeze co-solvent support polar-fluid continuity toward ~200 K.
D3: Water-processable co-binder can lower effective brittleness and preserve amorphous interfacial mobility below 253 K.
D4: Phosphoric acid can be used in complexed or partially neutralised/plasticised form rather than as a neat crystallising phase.
D5: 1-D fibrous or tubular clay supplies interconnected nanometric confinement for the hydrated acid fraction.
D6: Dense OH/SiOH/POx hydrogen-bonding sites create short proton-relay distances.
D7: Clay surface and polymer matrix can retain acid/water while avoiding fully immobilising the proton phase.

families.family_name: OH-rich polymer or biopolymer + 2-D layered aluminosilicate + buffered phosphoric-acid polar phase
families.family_description: This family uses layered clays to create high interfacial area and tortuous confinement rather than 1-D channels. It is a practical cold-side membrane route when the acid phase is buffered or co-solvated so that the layered galleries and polymer-clay interfaces host a non-freezing hydrogen-bonded proton medium.
descriptor_match: D1: Layered-clay/polymer interfaces can sustain continuous proton pathways if the acid-plasticiser phase remains distributed rather than phase-separated.
D2: Gallery-confined water/plasticiser and polymer-bound water help preserve low-temperature mobility.
D3: Amorphous polymer-rich interphases can reduce brittle channel disconnection at sub-zero temperatures.
D4: Buffered or co-solvated phosphoric-acid species are more suitable than neat acid for 182–299 K operation.
D5: Layered galleries provide nanoconfinement, though less directionally channelised than 1-D fibrous hosts.
D6: Polymer OH/NH and clay surface oxygens generate a dense hydrogen-bond landscape.
D7: Layered silicates typically improve acid and water retention by adsorption and tortuous diffusion paths.

families.family_name: Water-processable polymer matrix + phosphoric-acid deep-eutectic or polyol-complexed proton phase + inorganic nanofiller retainer
families.family_description: This archetype shifts the anti-freeze burden onto the proton phase itself by using glycerol-, glycol-, or choline-based complexation to suppress crystallisation of acid/water domains. An inorganic nanofiller is retained as an acid/water anchor and nanoconfinement aid, but the dominant low-temperature design lever is the complexed phosphoric-acid fluid.
descriptor_match: D1: Deep-eutectic or polyol-complexed acid phases are specifically intended to avoid disruptive freezing or eutectic segregation.
D2: Polyol-rich bound polar media can stay mobile well below 273 K.
D3: Plasticised polymer matrices are less likely to become glassy-brittle across the target window.
D4: Complexed phosphoric acid directly addresses the need for a cold-stable non-neat acid speciation.
D5: Nanofiller surfaces and polymer free volume provide distributed confinement of the conducting phase.
D6: Polyol/phosphate/polymer hydrogen-bond networks enable mixed vehicular and hopping transport.
D7: Filler and polymer together can reduce leakage of the liquid-like proton phase.

families.family_name: High-acid-affinity aromatic polymer control with phosphoric-acid complexation
families.family_description: This family is included as a control baseline rather than the main cold-side recommendation. Aromatic high-acid-affinity hosts can strongly bind phosphoric acid and form established proton-conducting complexes, but they are more often optimized for higher-temperature regimes and therefore mainly serve as a benchmark against which cold-side-friendly biopolymer/clay designs can be judged.
descriptor_match: D1: Strong acid-polymer complexation can preserve continuity of the proton phase, though low-temperature rigidification is a concern.
D2: Bound acid and residual water may persist, but polar-fluid mobility near 200 K is less favorable than in anti-freeze-plasticised systems.
D3: This descriptor is only partially matched because rigid aromatic matrices can become comparatively glassy at low temperature.
D4: Acid is complexed to the polymer rather than present as a separate neat phase.
D5: Confinement is molecular rather than via explicit 1-D or layered nanochannels.
D6: Imidazole- or basic-site-rich polymers provide dense proton-relay sites.
D7: Acid retention is usually strong, sometimes at the expense of proton mobility.

instances.instance_name: Chitosan / poly(vinyl alcohol) / sepiolite / phosphoric acid-glycerol-water membrane
instances.composition_description: Chitosan acts as the OH/NH-rich biopolymer matrix; poly(vinyl alcohol) is the water-processable film-forming co-binder that improves continuity and reduces brittleness; sepiolite provides 1-D fibrous nanochannels and interfacial acid retention; phosphoric acid is the proton donor; glycerol and residual water complex the acid phase and suppress low-temperature crystallisation. A practical starting formulation is chitosan:PVA = 60:40 by polymer mass, sepiolite = 10–25 wt% of total solids, and H3PO4 at 0.5–1.5 mol per mol chitosan repeat-unit amine equivalent with glycerol/H3PO4 mass ratio around 0.5–1.
expected_properties: conductivity_range: expected sub-zero proton conductivity in the 10^-5 to 10^-3 S/cm class depending on hydration and acid loading
acid_retention: moderate-to-good due to chitosan protonation and sepiolite surface adsorption
operating_temp: designed for 182–299 K with glycerol-assisted anti-freezing
mechanical_state: flexible cast membrane if glycerol and PVA are balanced against excessive acid loading
risk_flags: neat phosphoric acid domains may crystallise if glycerol/water ratio is insufficient
excess acid may over-plasticise and weaken film integrity
chitosan can become too water-sensitive at high acid loading

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: OH/NH-rich biopolymer host providing protonatable sites, bound water, and hydrogen-bond continuity
element_evidence.analog_reason: Chitosan is a standard proton-conducting biopolymer host and is a direct literature-class analog within the S08 fallback pool.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Water-processable co-binder improving film formation, amorphous continuity, and low-temperature flexibility
element_evidence.analog_reason: PVA is a widely used hydrophilic film-former for acid-containing proton-conductive membranes and is represented in the S08 fallback pool.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: 1-D fibrous clay supplying nanoconfined interfacial pathways and acid/water retention sites
element_evidence.analog_reason: Sepiolite is a recognized fibrous nanochannel clay analog in proton-conducting composite contexts in the S08 fallback pool.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Primary proton donor forming hydrogen-bonded phosphate networks with polymer, clay, glycerol, and water
element_evidence.analog_reason: Phosphoric-acid complexation is a core literature motif for proton conduction and is supported by acid-complex membrane cards in S08.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Anti-freeze co-solvent and plasticiser that complexes acid/water and suppresses rigidification
element_evidence.analog_reason: Glycerol is a standard low-temperature plasticising and anti-freeze polyol analog represented in the S08 fallback set.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Hydrogen-bonded proton-transfer medium associated with polymer, clay, and phosphate species
element_evidence.analog_reason: Bound water as the conducting co-medium is a generic but central analog in hydrated proton-conducting membrane literature represented in S08 fallback.

instances.novelty_rationale: Relative to the closest single-paper archetypes in manual_1157b11126, manual_1190463586, and manual_1ca1249fc4, this route explicitly combines biopolymer host, film-forming co-binder, 1-D fibrous clay, and glycerol-complexed phosphoric acid into one cold-side-targeted quaternary membrane. The mechanistic value is that glycerol addresses D1/D2/D4 directly while sepiolite addresses D5/D7 and the chitosan/PVA pair addresses D3 and fabrication practicality. Each component has its own element-level analog in the S08 pool, but the assembled low-temperature synergy is presented here as a new combination rather than a copied recipe.

instances.instance_name: Corn-starch / poly(vinyl alcohol) / attapulgite / phosphoric acid-ethylene glycol-water membrane
instances.composition_description: Corn starch provides an OH-rich polysaccharide matrix with bound-water affinity; PVA acts as the co-binder and crystallinity suppressor; attapulgite (palygorskite) provides 1-D fibrous nanoconfinement; phosphoric acid supplies protons; ethylene glycol depresses freezing and helps maintain acid/plasticiser continuity. A practical screening composition is starch:PVA = 50:50 to 70:30, attapulgite = 5–20 wt% of solids, H3PO4 = 20–50 wt% of polymer mass, and ethylene glycol = 10–40 wt% of polymer mass.
expected_properties: conductivity_range: expected 10^-6 to 10^-3 S/cm over 182–299 K depending on residual water and acid/plasticiser ratio
acid_retention: moderate, enhanced by attapulgite adsorption and starch/PVA hydrogen bonding
operating_temp: cold-side targeted with glycol-assisted freezing suppression
film_formability: good by water casting if starch gelatinisation and PVA dissolution are properly controlled
risk_flags: starch retrogradation may create heterogeneous domains on storage
excess ethylene glycol may increase leaching
attapulgite dispersion quality strongly affects percolation

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: OH-rich biopolymer matrix furnishing bound-water sites and dense hydrogen-bond donors/acceptors
element_evidence.analog_reason: Starch-based proton-conductive or hydrophilic composite membranes are represented as a biopolymer analog in the S08 fallback pool.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Film-forming co-binder that improves continuity and reduces brittleness of starch-rich membranes
element_evidence.analog_reason: PVA is a standard hydrophilic co-binder analog in proton-conducting membrane literature present in S08 fallback.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: 1-D fibrous clay channel and acid/water retainer generating nanometric confinement
element_evidence.analog_reason: Attapulgite/palygorskite is a recognized 1-D fibrous clay analog in the S08 fallback literature set.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Proton donor establishing phosphate-mediated transport pathways through the hydrated/plasticised network
element_evidence.analog_reason: Phosphoric-acid-based proton conduction is an established element in S08 fallback literature.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Anti-freeze co-solvent reducing freezing and maintaining mobile hydrogen-bonded fluidity
element_evidence.analog_reason: Ethylene glycol is a standard anti-freeze plasticiser analog for low-temperature hydrated systems and is represented in the S08 fallback pool.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Co-conducting hydrogen-bonded medium associated with starch, PVA, clay, glycol, and phosphate
element_evidence.analog_reason: Hydration-mediated proton transport is a generic literature analog reflected in S08 fallback cards.

instances.novelty_rationale: Relative to the closest single-paper starch-only, PVA-only, or clay-only formulations in the S08 fallback set, this instance makes a deliberate low-temperature combination of starch, PVA, attapulgite, and glycol-complexed phosphoric acid. The mechanistic value is that the starch/PVA pair broadens the amorphous hydrogen-bond network, while attapulgite adds 1-D confinement and glycol directly addresses cold-side phase stability. This is therefore a novel combination built from individually literature-familiar elements rather than a duplication of one known recipe.

instances.instance_name: Hydroxypropyl cellulose / poly(vinyl pyrrolidone) / halloysite nanotube / phosphoric acid-choline chloride-glycerol membrane
instances.composition_description: Hydroxypropyl cellulose serves as a low-crystallinity cellulose derivative host; poly(vinyl pyrrolidone) acts as a water-processable film former and acid-compatible co-binder; halloysite nanotubes provide tubular 1-D confinement; phosphoric acid is the proton source; choline chloride plus glycerol forms a deep-eutectic-like anti-freeze complexing medium around the acid phase. A reasonable first screen is HPC:PVP = 60:40, HNT = 5–15 wt%, phosphoric acid:choline chloride near 1:1 to 2:1 molar, with glycerol as a secondary plasticiser.
expected_properties: conductivity_range: expected 10^-5 to 10^-3 S/cm class if deep-eutectic acid phase remains well distributed
acid_retention: good due to PVP acid affinity and halloysite lumen/surface adsorption
operating_temp: intended for 182–299 K with anti-crystallisation support from choline chloride and glycerol
morphology: tubular-clay nanocomposite with polymer-rich continuous phase
risk_flags: deep-eutectic stoichiometry may strongly affect viscosity and conductivity
halloysite loading above percolation optimum may embrittle the film
choline chloride may increase hygroscopicity and composition drift

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: OH-rich cellulose-derivative host with reduced crystallinity and improved low-temperature flexibility
element_evidence.analog_reason: Cellulose-derivative hydrophilic membrane hosts are represented in the S08 fallback set and are appropriate analogs for HPC.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Water-processable co-binder providing film formation and strong hydrogen-bonding/acid compatibility
element_evidence.analog_reason: PVP is a well-known hydrophilic membrane former and acid-complexing polymer analog in the S08 fallback pool.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Tubular clay nanofiller generating 1-D confinement and interfacial retention of the proton phase
element_evidence.analog_reason: Halloysite nanotubes are a direct tubular-clay analog represented in the S08 fallback literature.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Primary proton donor forming mobile phosphate-rich hydrogen-bond networks
element_evidence.analog_reason: Phosphoric-acid complex proton conductors are supported by S08 fallback literature.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Deep-eutectic-forming salt that suppresses crystallisation and stabilises a polar proton medium at low temperature
element_evidence.analog_reason: Choline-chloride-containing deep eutectic or strongly hydrogen-bonded liquid phases are represented as low-temperature polar-medium analogs in S08 fallback.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Secondary anti-freeze plasticiser widening the non-crystallising composition window
element_evidence.analog_reason: Glycerol is a standard anti-freeze plasticiser analog in S08 fallback literature.

instances.novelty_rationale: The closest S08 archetypes support cellulose derivatives, PVP, halloysite, phosphoric acid, and deep-eutectic/plasticiser motifs individually, but not this specific six-component cold-side assembly. What is new is the simultaneous use of a low-crystallinity cellulose derivative, an amide-rich co-binder, a tubular nanoconfinement phase, and a choline chloride/glycerol-complexed phosphoric acid medium. That combination is mechanistically valuable because it attacks D3, D4, and D5 in parallel rather than relying on only one of those levers.

instances.instance_name: Chitosan / montmorillonite / potassium dihydrogen phosphate / glycerol / water membrane
instances.composition_description: Chitosan is the hydrophilic proton-relay host; montmorillonite supplies layered nanoconfinement and water retention; potassium dihydrogen phosphate provides a buffered phosphate proton source less prone to neat-acid crystallisation than pure H3PO4; glycerol depresses freezing and maintains plasticisation. A starting composition is chitosan with 3–10 wt% MMT, 10–30 wt% KH2PO4 relative to polymer, and 10–30 wt% glycerol.
expected_properties: conductivity_range: likely lower than free-acid systems but potentially more stable across freeze-thaw, around 10^-6 to 10^-4 S/cm
acid_retention: high because phosphate is buffered and non-volatile
operating_temp: favorable for sub-zero stability due to buffered phosphate and glycerol
dimensional_stability: improved by layered clay reinforcement
risk_flags: conductivity may be too low if phosphate is over-neutralised
MMT restacking can reduce effective gallery accessibility
salt-rich membranes may become brittle if under-plasticised

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Hydrophilic biopolymer host with protonatable amines and bound-water affinity
element_evidence.analog_reason: Chitosan is a direct biopolymer-host analog in the S08 fallback pool.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Layered clay nanofiller creating gallery confinement and enhancing retention of water/phosphate species
element_evidence.analog_reason: Montmorillonite is a standard layered-clay analog represented in the S08 fallback set.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Buffered phosphate proton source intended to avoid neat phosphoric-acid crystallisation
element_evidence.analog_reason: Acid-salt or phosphate-buffered proton media are represented in the S08 fallback literature and support KH2PO4 as a component-level analog.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Anti-freeze plasticiser preserving polar-fluid continuity and matrix flexibility
element_evidence.analog_reason: Glycerol is a direct low-temperature plasticiser analog in the S08 fallback set.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Hydrogen-bonded co-medium for phosphate-mediated proton transport
element_evidence.analog_reason: Hydrated proton transport is a generic analog represented in S08 fallback literature.

instances.novelty_rationale: Compared with the closest chitosan-acid or polymer-layered-clay formulations in S08 fallback, this route replaces a neat-acid emphasis with a buffered dihydrogen-phosphate strategy tailored to D4 under 182–299 K conditions. The difference matters mechanistically because low-temperature phase stability can be better when the proton source is already in a non-neat phosphate speciation and the layered clay helps retain the plasticised aqueous phase. This is therefore a novel combination emphasizing cold stability over maximum room-temperature conductivity.

instances.instance_name: Poly(vinyl alcohol) / silica / phosphoric acid-choline chloride-glycerol deep-eutectic-like membrane
instances.composition_description: PVA is the continuous water-processable matrix; nanosilica acts as a high-surface-area acid/water retainer and nanoconfinement aid; phosphoric acid is complexed with choline chloride and glycerol to create a cold-stable proton medium with reduced crystallisation tendency. A practical starting point is PVA with 5–15 wt% silica and an acid:choline chloride:glycerol molar ratio near 2:1:2, adjusted to preserve castability.
expected_properties: conductivity_range: expected 10^-5 to 10^-3 S/cm if the complexed proton phase remains continuous
acid_retention: moderate-to-good via silica adsorption and PVA hydrogen bonding
operating_temp: designed for broad non-freezing operation from ~182 K to room temperature
processing: straightforward aqueous casting followed by controlled drying
risk_flags: silica may over-bind water and increase viscosity if loading is too high
phase separation is possible if deep-eutectic fraction exceeds polymer compatibility limit
long-term hygroscopic drift may alter conductivity

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Hydrophilic film-forming matrix supporting acid complexation and flexible membrane casting
element_evidence.analog_reason: PVA is a direct analog for hydrophilic proton-conductive cast membranes in S08 fallback.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Nanofiller retainer and confinement aid for the complexed acid phase
element_evidence.analog_reason: Silica is a standard inorganic nanofiller analog for acid/water retention in proton-conductive composites represented in S08 fallback.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Proton donor integrated into a deep-eutectic-like hydrogen-bonded liquid phase
element_evidence.analog_reason: Phosphoric-acid-complex proton conductors are supported in S08 fallback literature.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Hydrogen-bond-accepting salt used to complex acid and suppress crystallisation
element_evidence.analog_reason: Choline-chloride-based low-freezing polar media are represented as component-level analogs in S08 fallback.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Polyol anti-freeze plasticiser widening the cold-stable liquid composition range
element_evidence.analog_reason: Glycerol is a direct anti-freeze/plasticiser analog in the S08 fallback pool.

instances.novelty_rationale: The closest S08 single-paper routes appear to treat polymer matrices, silica retainers, or deep-eutectic-like proton media separately rather than in this exact combination. Here the novelty is the deliberate use of a choline chloride/glycerol-complexed phosphoric-acid phase inside a PVA/silica membrane to directly target D1, D2, and D4 for the 182–299 K window. Each ingredient is individually literature-familiar, but the integrated cold-side design logic is combination-level novelty.

instances.composition_description: Polybenzimidazole serves as a high-acid-affinity aromatic host; phosphoric acid is absorbed to form the classical acid-base proton-conducting complex. This control is intentionally simple and does not include explicit anti-freeze co-solvent or clay nanoconfinement.
expected_properties: conductivity_range: good at elevated temperature, but likely poor or sharply reduced near the cold end of 182 K without special plasticisation
acid_retention: high due to strong acid-base complexation
operating_temp: included mainly as a high-temperature-oriented control baseline, not a preferred cold-side candidate
mechanical_state: robust film, but low-temperature rigidity is a concern
risk_flags: poor match to D2 and D3 at deep sub-zero temperatures
neat or weakly complexed phosphoric acid may not remain adequately mobile at the cold end
should not dominate the top-list because it is a control rather than a cold-side-optimized design

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Basic aromatic polymer host strongly complexing phosphoric acid
element_evidence.analog_reason: PBI is a direct literature-class analog in the S08 fallback pool for phosphoric-acid-complex membranes.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Primary proton donor in the classical PBI-PA acid-base complex
element_evidence.analog_reason: Phosphoric acid is the canonical proton donor component in the S08 fallback literature for PBI-type membranes.

instances.novelty_rationale: This is retained as an exact-match control baseline rather than as a novel candidate. Its value is that PBI-phosphoric acid is a widely recognized reference point for acid-complex proton conduction and can anchor expectations for acid retention and benchmark conductivity trends. Including it helps the downstream ranker distinguish genuinely cold-side-improved designs from a classical high-temperature membrane that is expected to underperform near the 182–253 K region.
